alternatives.option: Embed an 8-bit `DataOrigin` character tag instead of key-type metadata.
alternatives.whyRejected: An origin tag does not identify the record-id and child-id CLR types needed to deserialize or validate a `ShardKey` when the generic type arguments are not known in advance.

alternatives.option: Serialize `ShardKey` values without any type metadata header.
alternatives.whyRejected: Deserialization could not detect mismatched generic type arguments, and untyped diagnostic or grain-key consumers (`GhostShardKey`) could not inspect serialized keys without compile-time type knowledge.

fields.consequences: Deserializing a `ShardKey` with mismatched generic type arguments throws `InvalidShardKeyMetadataException`, and `GhostShardKey` can reconstruct and format a serialized key without compile-time type arguments. Equality comparisons (`Equals`, `GetHashCode`, `==`) compare only `ShardId` and the typed key values, ignoring the metadata header.
fields.context: Serialized `ShardKey` values flow through channels where the reader may not know the generic key-column types at compile time (such as structured logging and Orleans grain identity strings) or where mismatched generic type arguments must be detected on deserialization.
fields.decision: Every `ShardKey` carries compact `ShardKeyTypeMetadata` encoding the arity and .NET `ShardKeyType` of its record-id and child-id components. This metadata header is written at the front of every serialized representation (binary, UTF-8, and external string) and validated when deserializing into a typed `ShardKey<...>`. Equality compares only the `ShardId` and key component values.
fields.title: Embed key-type metadata in serialized shard keys
